note: INTERACTIVE WALKTHROUGH AND DETERMINISTIC SIMULATION RUNTIME FOUNDATION — READ-ONLY INTERACTION ONLY. This layer reads the derived visual scene and produces an ephemeral runtime scene and runtime state: walkable surfaces, obstacles, portals, interaction capabilities, a spatial index, selection, visibility, measurement and camera state. It never writes to the visual scene and never writes to any canonical engineering model. It ships no simulation engine: no evacuation, no crowds, no fire or smoke, no CFD, no thermal, no structural analysis, no vehicle or robot behaviour, no AI, no pathfinding agents and no physics engine.
derivation_note: the runtime scene is DERIVED from the visual scene, which is itself derived from the canonical engineering model. The flow is one-way — CANONICAL -> COORDINATION -> VISUAL -> RUNTIME SCENE -> RUNTIME STATE -> USER INTERACTION — and no runtime value is ever written back into any upstream layer.
ephemerality_note: RUNTIME IS EPHEMERAL. ENGINEERING MODEL IS IMMUTABLE. A selection, a hidden object, an open door, a measurement, a camera position and a simulation clock are session state. None of them is a model fact, none of them survives into a revision hash, and none of them may be presented as an engineering decision.
navigation_note: these are navigation CONTRACTS, not a character controller and not a physics engine. WALK states that gravity and collision apply and that a walkable surface is required; FLY states explicitly that gravity does not apply and that its collision policy is its own rather than inherited from WALK. No claim of realistic character physics, input feel or latency is made anywhere.
capsule_note: the player is a validated capsule, never a zero-volume camera point. Every default lives here in the canonical specification rather than as a hidden constant in code. A capsule must satisfy: radius and height finite and strictly positive and inside the declared limits, height strictly greater than twice the radius, and eye height strictly greater than zero and not greater than the height.

DOOR.basis: an opening in its host wall; passability is decided by its portal state

WINDOW.basis: a modelled opening that is glazed rather than passable

SLAB.basis: modelled floor plate; supports the capsule

CEILING.basis: overhead surface, not an obstacle at capsule height

ROOF_CAP.basis: visual-only cap; never an engineering surface

EQUIPMENT.basis: modelled MEP equipment occupying floor volume

RISER.basis: modelled MEP riser occupying floor volume

SEGMENT.basis: modelled MEP route, declared non-blocking for walkthrough

TERMINAL.basis: modelled MEP terminal, declared non-blocking for walkthrough

GROUND.basis: visual-only ground plane; never a site boundary and never a walkable engineering surface

collision_policy_note: collision behaviour is DECLARED here per object kind, never inferred from a mesh name, a material, an asset or a size. A kind that is absent from this table falls back to the default policy for its layer and is reported, so an unclassified kind can never silently become solid or silently become passable.
decoration_note: decoration and other visual-only objects are NON_BLOCKING by default and never become engineering geometry, a structural obstacle, an MEP object, a fire/life-safety object or a room boundary. A caller may explicitly declare decoration BLOCKING for a runtime session; that choice is recorded on the runtime scene, applies to visual-only furniture only, and still creates no engineering fact.
visual_only_note: a visual-only object may be selectable, inspectable as visual metadata and hideable. It never gains an engineering source, a discipline fact or a canonical property through the runtime, and inspecting it returns visual metadata explicitly labelled as such.
walkable_note: walkable surfaces are derived from canonical spaces — each space contributes one surface at its level elevation, bounded by the space rectangle the architectural layer already publishes. Browser triangle guessing is never the source of truth. Where a slab object exists at that level it is recorded as the supporting element; where none exists the surface still exists but records support_element_id as null rather than inventing one.
portal_state_note: OPEN and CLOSED are the only canonical runtime portal states. Changing one changes RUNTIME STATE alone: the engineering door is untouched, its hash is unchanged, and no access control, security, locking or scheduling behaviour is implied or implemented.
portal_connectivity_note: connectivity is derived geometrically from canonical data only: the door's own world position is inverse-transformed into model space and probed against the canonical space rectangles on its level, on both sides of its host wall. Two spaces found gives a room-to-room portal; one space found on an exterior-exposed host wall gives a room-to-exterior portal; anything else is reported UNRESOLVED. Connectivity is never fabricated to complete a graph.
vertical_connection_note: a vertical connection is recorded where the canonical model already states one — a stair core serving more than one level. Ramps are recorded on the same contract when the model states them. Lifts and escalators are NOT simulated: no elevator operation, call logic, travel time or capacity exists in this phase, and none is implied.
action_note: every action has declared valid target kinds, deterministic behaviour on an invalid target, and a runtime-only effect. No action writes to a model: writes_to_model is structurally false on every action result, and an action shaped like a model write is refused with RUNTIME_MODEL_WRITE_ATTEMPT.
capability_note: capabilities travel on the runtime object through a deterministic contract. The interface never guesses a capability from a mesh name, a material or a layer string.
visibility_note: visibility is ephemeral runtime state held as an explicit hidden set on the RuntimeState. Nothing is deleted, no canonical element is removed, and no persisted model field is written. RESTORE_VISIBILITY clears the set exactly.
discipline_note: the runtime reuses the canonical visual layer vocabulary as its discipline vocabulary rather than inventing a competing enum. A discipline outside this list is refused.
measurement_note: a measurement is runtime-only and carries runtime_only: true structurally. Distance is always computed from validated coordinates or from validated source geometry — a caller-supplied distance is never trusted and never echoed. A measurement is never a code check, a clearance requirement or a compliance statement.
spatial_index_note: max_abs_coordinate_m bounds what may be indexed at all. A coordinate beyond it is not a building coordinate; it is refused for indexing rather than expanded into cells, so a hostile box can never be turned into an unbounded cell enumeration.

a uniform spatial hash over the runtime obstacles and walkable surfaces. A movement, spawn or pick query resolves candidates from the cells it touches rather than scanning every runtime object; an entry spanning more than the declared cell budget is placed in an oversized list compared against everything, so no candidate is ever lost and the count is reported rather than hidden.
issue_order_note: issues are emitted in a deterministic order — severity rank, then code, then subject, then detail — so the Python and browser implementations produce the same issue-code sequence for the same invalid input. No map iteration order, filesystem order or hash order reaches the output.
model_write_note: the runtime exposes no path that could set a wall width, move a wall, delete a door, change room geometry, change a beam, modify a pipe, move a fire device, add an engineering object, rewrite a source id or write an engineering coordinate. Any action carrying such an intent is refused with RUNTIME_MODEL_WRITE_ATTEMPT, and the runtime holds only deep copies so that mutating a runtime structure cannot reach source state through a shared reference.
determinism_note: every runtime identifier is derived from stable source identifiers and the runtime object kind. No wall-clock time, no random source, no UUID, no process address and no iteration-order-dependent value enters an identifier or any parity-critical field. The runtime scene carries no generated_at timestamp.
simulation_time_note: simulation_time exists on the runtime state as a finite, non-negative clock and as a foundation only. Advancing it changes nothing else: no evacuation, no occupancy, no heat, no smoke, no equipment and no agent behaviour is attached to it in this phase, and none is implied.
rule_note: factual runtime counts only. Nothing here is a regulatory input, no runtime count is compared to a threshold, and no runtime value feeds a code evaluation.
no_engine_note: this phase ships NO simulation engine, NO physics engine, NO pathfinding, NO agents, NO AI, NO network transport and NO geometry authoring. It answers how the compiled building may be walked, selected, inspected, hidden and measured — never what the building should be.
